id: loom-redact-by-shape-before-truncate
title: Redact credential shapes before truncating transcript-derived artifacts
scope: loom
type: decision
status: candidate
tag: human
sources:
  - session: 5c37b3b4-fb29-4e2e-8468-f63119e0d930
    project: loom
    date: 2026-09-15
    role: documented existing project decision on transcript redaction ordering
related: []
recorded_at: 2026-09-15
---

## Choice

Shape-based redaction of transcript-derived artifacts runs before tool-result truncation, and credential detection uses recognizable shape patterns rather than entropy filtering.

## Alternatives

Entropy-based secret detection, or truncating tool results before redacting them.

## Rationale

Shape-based patterns are deterministic and testable, preserve evidentiary identifiers that entropy filtering would erase, and centralize redaction policy at a single choke point. Truncating first risks shortening a secret below its pattern's minimum detectable length, letting it pass through unredacted.

## Principle

When both truncation and redaction apply to the same data, redact first — truncation can destroy the signal a detector needs, but redaction never needs the full untruncated length to be effective.

===END-OF-DECISION===
---
id: loom-single-entry-point-knowledge-writes
title: Route all knowledge-store writes through one Go entry point
scope: loom
type: decision
status: candidate
tag: human
sources:
  - session: 5c37b3b4-fb29-4e2e-8468-f63119e0d930
    project: loom
    date: 2026-09-15
    role: documented existing project decision on knowledge-store write path
related: []
recorded_at: 2026-09-15
---

## Choice

Every write to `~/.loom/knowledge` goes through a single entry point: Go callers use `internal/knowledge/store` directly, and Python callers must delegate through the `loom knowledge write` CLI command rather than reimplementing store or Git logic.

## Alternatives

Letting Python callers write to the knowledge store's git repo directly, duplicating the commit/push logic in each language.

## Rationale

Committing and pushing are properties of the single entry point itself, not of the caller, which guarantees every mutation is path-scoped and consistently versioned. Allowing multiple write paths would risk callers omitting Git handling or diverging in behavior. The accepted cost is that Python-side knowledge writes require the Loom binary to be present.

## Principle

When a resource requires an invariant on every write (here: commit + push), enforce it by funneling all writers through one implementation rather than trusting each caller to replicate it.

===END-OF-DECISION===
